<issue>
Last entity wins naming convention
Now by default the 1st name takes precedent when reading in entity definitions, all others with same name after the fact in the entity file(s) are considered redundant and ignored.

This being changed to make the last name read in files to take precedent instead. This would make @includes in your entity definitions far more useful.

This change is actually the same behavior hammer uses.

Thank you! 

</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

content.text:
I changed duplicate handling so the last definition of an entity name now wins instead of the first. I haven't built it or run any tests, and I didn't add or update any tests.

The change is in `filterRedundantClasses` in `lib/TbMdlLib/src/EntityDefinitionParser.cpp`. It now walks the class list from the end and reverses the kept results at the end, so the original order is preserved. Because `@include` contents are spliced into the same list at the point of the include, a definition later in the file overrides one from an earlier include, as in Hammer.

The existing exception still applies: a point class and a brush class with the same name can coexist. The "Duplicate class info" and "Redundant class info" warnings are still emitted, but they now refer to the earlier definition rather than the later one.

The doc comment above `filterRedundantClasses` still says a class is redundant if the same name appears "at an earlier position". That is now backwards and I didn't update it. Existing tests that expect first-wins behaviour will also fail and need updating.
